Two of the GTA V references (GTAV-02 and GTAV-05) carry a logo watermark, and our frames carry our HUD.. Judge: A is better in all four pairs, and none is close. The A frames are finished and coherent: strong lighting (moonlit stained glass, hard sun with crisp shadows), dense surface detail (grass blades, chain-link shadows, graffiti and peeling paint, glossy reflective car paint and chrome) and deliberate, cinematic framing, although pair 4's A is sparse on people and traffic. Two A frames (pair 1's night close-up and pair 3's low-angle pursuit shot) genuinely wow. None of the B frames do. The B frames share the same problems in every pair, so these are pipeline-level gaps rather than one-off issues. First, the hero character is low fidelity: blocky, posterized forearm skin, stiff locked-elbow aiming, hands and pistol that cannot be read, a plasticky face and matte cloth without folds. Second, placeholder or broken assets are visible: blank green sign panels, a chrome-hoop object on the walkway, a floating street-name label and a minimap that is an empty grid. Third, exposure is hazy and low in contrast, and road shadows are smeary and low resolution. Fourth, firing effects are crude: an offset orange muzzle smear and thin tracers. Fifth, compositions are weak, with the HUD covering the character and police and threats barely readable. The setting has real promise: shophouse arcades with Peranakan tiles, a hawker centre, a landmark skyline and warm golden-hour light. In priority order, closing the gap means: (1) a character and weapon pass on arms, hands, grip pose, cloth folds and pistol detail, (2) replacing every placeholder asset and the empty minimap, (3) a lighting and exposure pass for contrast, shadow resolution and contact shadows, (4) more traffic, pedestrians and police that read clearly (a liveried car with a light bar), and (5) muzzle effects anchored to the barrel tip.
